# @zakkster/lite-signal-dom

> Zero-GC, vanilla-first reactive DOM bindings for @zakkster/lite-signal. No virtual DOM, no template compiler, no build step. Each binding is one lite-signal `effect` wrapping a single DOM property write; the getter is captured once at bind time, so the per-update hot path allocates nothing. A keyed list reconciler diffs by key, reuses surviving elements, and recycles removed ones through a pool.

## Install
npm i @zakkster/lite-signal-dom
Peer dependency: @zakkster/lite-signal ^1.5.0-rc.1 (keyed uses its runWithOwner ownership scope). ESM only. Ships .d.ts.

## Mental model
- A "binding" ties one DOM property/attribute/class/style/event to a reactive getter.
- Every binding returns an idempotent `dispose()` handle.
- Bindings ALSO auto-dispose when their element leaves the DOM, via one shared document-level MutationObserver. A same-tick remove+re-insert (reorder/recycle) is detected via `isConnected` and does NOT dispose.
- Reads inside a getter must be lite-signal reads (`signal()`, `computed()`); writes (`.set`, `.update`) trigger the bound update synchronously.

## API
All getters are `() => value`. All binders return `() => void` (dispose).

bindText(node, getter): set node.textContent. Safe. Coerces to string.
bindHTMLUnsafe(node, getter): set node.innerHTML. UNSAFE — never pass untrusted input.
bindAttr(node, attr, getter): set/remove attribute. null|undefined|false => removeAttribute; true => "" (boolean attr); else String(value).
bindProp(node, prop, getter): set live DOM property (value, checked, ...). Use for form state.
bindClass(node, className, getter): toggle one class on truthy/falsy; leaves other classes alone.
bindStyle(node, styleProp, getter): set inline style prop; null|undefined resets to "".
bindShow(node, getter, displayStyle=""): show/hide via style.display (shown => displayStyle, hidden => "none").
bindOn(node, eventName, handler, options?): addEventListener tied to DOM lifetime. touchstart/touchmove/wheel/mousewheel default to {passive:true}; pass options to override.
keyed(parent, listGetter, keyFn, renderFn): keyed list reconciler. Returns dispose for the whole list.
  - listGetter: () => array (reactive).
  - keyFn: (item) => string|number, stable & unique per render.
  - renderFn: (item, recycledElement|null) => { element, dispose }. Build a new element or reset the recycled one. renderFn reads are untracked, so the list effect re-runs only when the LIST changes; per-row reactivity comes from bindings set inside renderFn.

## Guarantees / edge cases
- ~0 bytes allocated per update for simple bindings and for keyed reorders. Measured in isolation (no-op DOM, no observer) to separate library cost from host-DOM cost: < 0.02 bytes/update over 1,000,000 bindText updates and 100,000 keyed reorders. In a browser the only extra per-update cost is the native DOM mutation itself.
- keyed diff is a 3-pass integer-epoch mark-sweep: no Set, no key array, no iterators allocated per update. The key-scratch buffer is truncated when the list shrinks, so old keys are not retained.
- IN-PLACE ARRAY REUSE: re-setting the same mutated array reference bails under the default Object.is equality (the reconciler won't run). Use a fresh array, or signal(arr, { equals: false }) for zero-allocation reorders.
- Keys must be unique per render; duplicates collapse to one view (last position wins).
- Disposal is idempotent (call dispose any number of times).
- Auto-disposal covers an element and its bound descendants. Raw text-node bindings removed directly are not auto-collected — bind on the parent element or call dispose manually.
- SSR/no-DOM safe at import: the observer is only constructed where MutationObserver exists, and armed lazily on the first binding.

## Bundle
~1.7 KB min+gzip. Zero dependencies beyond @zakkster/lite-signal.

## Example
import { signal } from "@zakkster/lite-signal";
import { bindText, bindOn, keyed } from "@zakkster/lite-signal-dom";

const count = signal(0);
bindText(label, () => `count: ${count()}`);
bindOn(button, "click", () => count.update(n => n + 1));

const todos = signal([{ id: 1, text: signal("first") }]);
keyed(listEl, todos, t => t.id, (t, recycled) => {
  const li = recycled || document.createElement("li");
  return { element: li, dispose: bindText(li, () => t.text()) };
});
